Subject: Novarx MAP: proposed perf evaluation and timeline

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time today — good alignment on the priority use cases (interactive assistant + batch reranking). As discussed, I put together a short Mutual Action Plan to run a focused performance evaluation across our three hosting modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private VPC). The goal: baseline latency, throughput, TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency behavior under Novarx-like request patterns, and capture autoscaling/isolation differences.

High-level MAP items:
- Week 0 (this week): confirm test dataset (2k representative requests + 200 long-form prompts) and SLO targets.
- Week 1: Redwood runs hosted baseline (10k tokens/min sustained, 5 concurrent clients), capture TTFT + p95/p99 latencies.
- Week 2: Dedicated pool run with reserved capacity mirroring Novarx expected QPS; test burst behavior and autoscale.
- Week 3: Private VPC run (customer-provisioned infra) to validate isolation and end-to-end networking impact.
- Deliverable: perf CSV + short executive summary, recommended hosting mode for rollout, and rollout timeline for procurement.

Can you confirm the dataset by EOD tomorrow and share any specific SLOs you want measured (e.g., p99 < 800ms for interactive)? If you prefer, we'll run an initial hosted smoke test this week to sanity-check the harness.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Alex,

Thanks — this looks great and aligned with our internal timeline. Quick answers:
- Dataset: please use the anonymized 2k user requests from our May export (I uploaded to the secure folder: elena/novarx/bench/may2027).
- Targets: for interactive assistant we want p95 < 600ms and p99 < 1s under typical load (5–10 concurrent clients). For batch reranking, throughput is more important: 2500 documents/min sustained with latency per doc < 300ms.
- Week 3 (Private) might be tight for procurement; can we run the Private run in parallel with Dedicated if Redwood can coordinate with our infra team?

Also, can you include TTFT measured from TCP handshake to first token? That metric matters for our UX engineering team.

Appreciate it — cc'ing our IT lead so we can unblock access where needed.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-07-02T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novarx MAP: proposed perf evaluation and timeline

Alex / Marissa / Elena — quick status from execution team. We executed the harness across Hosted and Dedicated this week; Private run is scheduled for tomorrow with Novarx IT. Summary below (full CSV attached).

Summary highlights (short):
- Hosted (baseline): interactive profile (5 concurrent clients)
  - p50 TTFT: 85ms
  - p95 latency: 410ms
  - p99 latency: 720ms
  - sustained throughput: ~1,800 tokens/s (~108k tokens/min)
  - Notes: TTFT measured from TCP handshake outbound from Redwood client VM to first token returned.

- Dedicated (reserved pool sized to 8x baseline VM):
  - p50 TTFT: 82ms
  - p95 latency: 370ms
  - p99 latency: 620ms
  - observed autoscale: on a synthetic 3x spike, additional workers added in 48s (steady-state throughput recovered in 90s).
  - isolation test: when we injected noisy tenants (CPU heavy) on co-located host, p99 increased by ~14% transiently; reserving extra headroom reduced variance.

Preliminary conclusion: both Hosted and Dedicated meet Novarx interactive p95 target of <600ms and p99 target <1s. Dedicated gives slightly better tail and faster sustained throughput; autoscale latency is measurable but within a minute. Private run tomorrow will highlight network/NAT overheads.

Attachments: novarx-map-benchmark-results.csv (CSV, 52KB), novarx-map-summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

I'll follow up after the Private run with a short appendix showing delta vs hosted/dedicated.

—Karthik
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

If Novarx is comfortable with these outcomes we'll prepare a Dedicated proposal (capacity sizing + optional burst) and a Private deployment checklist (KMS, IP allowlist, audit log retention).

Alex
